headline: Latvia's governing party heads for clear election win
deck: The prime minister's centrist party has 36 per cent with most votes counted; he rules out governing with the Trump-inspired runner-up.
extended: Andris Kulbergs, Latvia's prime minister, looks set to win Saturday's parliamentary election by a wide margin. With 84 per cent of the votes counted, his centrist party, United List, has 36 per cent, far more than polls before the vote suggested.

Latvia First, a party inspired by Donald Trump, the American president, and his Maga movement, is set to come second with 13.3 per cent. On Saturday evening Kulbergs ruled out a coalition with it and rejected any cooperation with pro-Russian parties.

Sovereign Power, a pro-Russian party, has 11.1 per cent and the National Alliance, a Latvian nationalist party, 9.3 per cent. The Progressive Party, led by Andris Spruds, a former defence minister, has 6.7 per cent and wants at least 5 per cent of GDP spent on defence.
The current coalition is United List, the National Alliance, New Unity and the Union of Greens and Farmers. The last two have between 5 and 6 per cent, against a threshold of 5 per cent.
Kulbergs said early on Saturday evening, after an exit poll gave the party 35.6 per cent: 'It is incredibly good. I had not expected such a result.'
